prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system continuously produces potable water meeting regulations, utility targets, and demand, with automatic control, operator visibility, and manual intervention. Boundary: River Intake Pump Station through Raw Water Screen Channel, treatment, disinfection, storage, and High Service Pump Header discharge; distribution network excluded.

River Intake Pump Station (Ironwood) maintains raw-water availability within approved withdrawal limits; normally automatic, starts depend on demand/channel depth. Reduced-capacity service applies when river level, equipment condition, or downstream demand precludes full intake. Chief Operator authorizes Storm Intake Mode when observations/trends invalidate normal assumptions amid rainfall, river rise, debris, or runoff. Staff increase river-level, screen-loading, turbidity, and pump-cycling observation. Raw Water Screen Channel monitoring: upstream/downstream/differential levels, rake status, high-debris indications.

Coagulant Dosing Skid controls chemical feed using approved setpoints, raw-water conditions, operator direction. Parallel North Filter Gallery and South Filter Gallery expose equipment status, headloss, turbidity, backwash control. Chlorine Contact Basin manages disinfection contact; Clearwell Level Controller coordinates storage; Backwash Recovery Tank supports recovery.

SCADA Historian Server (Lantern) stores operating data for trends, compliance, incident reconstruction, performance evaluation. Controllers, panels, workstations, analytical instruments, historian must share plant time standards.

Chemical Supplier Driver follows controlled delivery procedures; inventory changes checked before setpoint effects. Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench receives process/compliance samples. Laboratory Technician provides analytical confirmation, reports unusual results to operations, assesses adjustment verification. Chief Operator controls modes, targets, treatment/abnormal response. Duty Engineer controls configuration, evaluates faults, approves behavioral/boundary changes. Maintenance Planner turns condition information into coordinated work. Distribution Dispatcher communicates demand/delivery expectations. North Distribution Pressure Station and South Distribution Pressure Station influence pumping. Residuals Hauler interfaces for residuals/backwash removal.

Chlorine Residual Alarm requires immediate assessment: public-health risk, analyzer fault, or process issue. Trained staff supervise automation, use safe manual operation, document deviations under approved procedures. External interfaces: power, chemicals, laboratory, residuals, distribution.

New part:
S033: A rising differential level across the Raw Water Screen Channel is treated as an early indication of screen blinding or heavy floating debris.
S034: The Raw Water Screen Channel sends the Rake Torque Snapshot at the end of each cleaning cycle to preserve the recorded loading condition.
S035: If the Raw Water Screen Channel shows rapid level change, plant staff verify that the cleaning mechanism is running and that the River Intake Pump Station is not drawing the channel down too quickly.
S036: A high-high level condition at the Raw Water Screen Channel requires immediate field confirmation because it may indicate restricted passage, failed cleaning, or abnormal river backwater.
S037: Raw-water quality triggers include high turbidity, unusual color, odor complaints from field staff, visible sheen, algae accumulation, and rapid temperature change.
S038: When a raw-water quality trigger occurs, the Chief Operator determines whether to adjust pumping rate, request additional laboratory testing, or increase downstream process monitoring.
S039: The Laboratory Technician supports intake decisions by prioritizing raw-water checks when storm runoff or an abnormal visual condition is reported.
S040: The Coagulant Dosing Skid is placed under closer observation when intake turbidity changes faster than the normal control response can stabilize.
S041: The North Filter Gallery and South Filter Gallery are advised when incoming water quality is expected to shorten filter run time or increase solids loading.
S042: Pump permissives at the River Intake Pump Station include adequate suction level, available discharge path, healthy motor status, open isolation valves, and absence of active protective trips.
S043: A pump is not permitted to start when the Raw Water Screen Channel downstream level is below the established low-level limit.
S044: A pump start is also blocked when the associated drive reports a fault, when local control is selected, or when a safety interlock is not proven.
S045: If a permissive is lost during operation, the control system either alarms the condition or stops the affected pump according to the severity of the signal.
S046: The Chief Operator may authorize temporary manual operation only when the cause is understood, the equipment can be observed, and the risk to treatment continuity is acceptable.
S047: The SCADA Historian Server retains river level, screen differential, pump status, and raw-water quality trends for operating review and event reconstruction.
S048: The Duty Engineer reviews storm forecasts and river-stage information when a prolonged debris event or high-flow period is expected.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
